title: Italian: Essere, Avere & Friends
description: The two verbs everything else leans on, plus a handful of everyday action words and some classic "avere" expressions.

cards.details: Irregular and everywhere. Master its six forms and half of Italian opens up.
Italians usually drop *io*, because the verb already tells you who: *Sono stanco* = I'm tired.

cards.prompt: *Essere*: how do you say "you are" (informal, one person)?
cards.details: Same spelling as the number six, *sei*. You'll be fine; context saves you.
That accent matters: *è* = is, *e* = and. *Lei è italiana e simpatica.*
*Siamo in ritardo!* = we're late! Very common in Italy too.

cards.prompt: *Essere*: how do you say "you all are"?
cards.details: *Voi* is plural "you", like "you guys" or "y'all".
Identical to "I am" (*sono*)! Context, or adding *loro*, tells them apart.
Italian uses "to have" for lots of things English does with "to be": hunger, age, being right…
The *h* is silent: just "oh". It's there to tell *ho* (I have) apart from *o* (or).

cards.prompt: *Avere*: how do you say "you have" (informal, one person)?
cards.details: Pronounced "eye". *Hai fame?* = are you hungry?
Silent *h* again, so it's just "ah". Different from *a* (to/at).
The *-iamo* ending is "we" for almost every Italian verb. Spot it and you know who's talking.

cards.prompt: *Avere*: how do you say "you all have"?
cards.details: The *-ete* ending is the "you all" form for *-ere* verbs.
Not to be confused with *anno* (year). Double *nn*, silent *h*.
Wildly irregular: *vado, vai, va…* *Andiamo!* = let's go!
A workhorse verb: *fare una foto* (take a photo), *fare colazione* (have breakfast), *fa caldo* (it's hot).
Its polite cousin *vorrei* ("I would like") is the one to use when ordering.
*Posso?* ("May I?") is one of the most useful single words in Italian.
Behind the famous Italian-American "mangia!" (eat!), said by every grandmother ever.
Short and irregular: *bevo* (I drink). *Qualcosa da bere?* = something to drink?
A perfectly regular *-are* verb, the model for thousands of others: *parlo, parli, parla…*

cards.prompt: Using *avere*, how do you say "I'm hungry"?
cards.details: Literally "I have hunger". Same pattern: *ho sete* (I'm thirsty), *ho sonno* (I'm sleepy).

cards.prompt: Using *avere*, how do you say "I'm 30 years old"?
cards.details: You *have* your years in Italian. Saying *sono trenta* sounds like you're claiming to be thirty people!

cards.prompt: How do you say "there is" in Italian?
cards.details: From *ci* + *è*. *C'è un bar qui vicino?* = Is there a café near here?

cards.prompt: How do you say "there are" in Italian?
cards.details: Plural partner of *c'è*: *Ci sono due treni.* = There are two trains.
